title: Project Zomboid Agent Gameplay Knowledge Document
description: One knowledge/gameplay/*.yaml document: a set of gameplay rules the planner and the missions may consult. Every rule states where it came from and how far it has been verified; a rule without a source or with an unverifiable claim dressed as verified is refused by the loader, not corrected. The vocabulary is closed on purpose: free text lives only in the fields named for it, and every enum here is mirrored by the loader in pz_agent_core.knowledge.

domain.description: The knowledge area this document covers. Closed list; a new domain is a reviewed change to this schema and the loader together.

id.description: Stable rule identifier: domain-prefixed token, unique across the whole corpus.

build.description: The game build the claim is about, e.g. "42.20". A rule inherited from Build 41 lore must say 41 and can never be verified_live against 42.

source.description: Where the claim comes from, most authoritative applicable tier. code = this repository's shipped policy/adapter (name the path in source_detail); live_probe = a capability probe or live-session finding; official = The Indie Stone's published material; wiki = PZwiki, secondary by policy and never sufficient for verified status on its own.

source_detail.description: The exact place: a repo path with anchor, a live-run date, a URL. Required in spirit for every tier; the loader refuses code-sourced rules without a repo path here.

status.description: verified_live = a real session observed the postcondition; verified_script = the rule restates behaviour this repository's tested code enforces (source must be code); unverified = a claim nothing has proven yet. The loader refuses verified_live without a live evidence pointer in proven_by, and verified_script whose source is not code.

claim.description: The rule, one bounded human sentence.

observed_inputs.description: Observation fields the decision reads, as dotted paths into the observation document (e.g. player.stats.hunger, nearby.objects[].locked). Closed alphabet, bounded.

decision.description: The deterministic decision the rule encodes, as bounded prose naming the code that makes it when source is code.

actions.description: Protocol action names the rule drives, exactly as ActionName spells them; empty for observation-only rules.

on_failure.description: What replanning does when the postcondition does not hold, bounded prose; name reason codes where the code speaks them.

risk_class.description: The protocol risk tier the driven actions carry; P0 for observation-only rules.

goal_kinds.description: Goal kinds this rule serves, for bounded retrieval. Values must be GoalKind members; empty means the rule is general.

needs.description: Need channels this rule speaks to, for retrieval when a need is active.

nearby_kinds.description: Nearby-object kinds whose presence makes this rule relevant, for retrieval (door, corpse, container type tokens, zombie).

proven_by.description: What proves the rule at its declared status: repo test paths for verified_script; a live scenario id (S01..S20) or evidence-bundle pointer for verified_live; empty only for unverified.

numbers.description: Named numeric facts the rule relies on, each carrying its own honesty: a number with status unverified is a hypothesis the planner may not treat as ground truth.
